raw_case_text: A 37-year-old HIV-1 positive, antiretroviral therapy naive woman was admitted to the ICU with a history of a generalized maculopapular rash, joint pains, pyrexia, fatigue and delirium. She had been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection in 2006 and as per local guidelines at the time was never initiated on antiretroviral therapy as her CD4+ lymphocyte count had always been >500 cells/mul at regular clinic follow up. On examination, she appeared ill with a pyrexia of 39.1 C and a generalized maculopapular rash (Fig. 1). Her knee, elbow and ankle joints were markedly swollen. She was also found to have axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy, a 4 cm splenomegaly but no hepatomegaly. Except for features in keeping with delirium, no other abnormal neurological signs were noted. On this admission she had a CD4+ cell count of 616 cells/mul, a HIV viral load of 102 000 copies/mL and her HTLV-1 serology also tested strongly positive. Except for a markedly raised serum calcium level of 4.48 mmol/L, the rest of her laboratory work-up including full blood count, electrolytes, renal and liver function test, blood and urine culture, autoimmune screen, serum protein electrophoresis, serum angiotensin converting enzyme (S-ACE), parathyroid hormone (PTH) assay, beta-2 microglobulin, urinary Bence-Jones protein, joint fluid analysis and a nasopharangeal swab for the detection of respiratory viruses were unremarkable. A full body CAT scan showed extensive lymphadenopathy in the axillary, inguinal, pelvic and para-aortic regions. Radio-isotopic bone scanning showed increased uptake in the juxta-articular areas of the elbow and knee joints. Histology of a skin lesion biopsy showed a vasculitic infiltration of abnormal looking T cells, whilst lymph node biopsy and bone marrow aspiration and trephine specimens confirmed the diagnosis of acute ATLL. Her hypercalcaemia initially proved refractory to stepwise conventional calcium lowering therapy that included large volume saline diuresis (normal saline at 200 mL/h x 24 h, then 120 mL/h x 48h), loop diuretics (80 mg of furosemide 12h x 3 days), corticosteroids (100 mg of hydrocortisone 8h x 3 days) and intravenous bisphosphonate therapy (4 mg of zolendronic acid over 15 min x 1 dose). On the fifth day, due to a lack of improvement in the degree of hypercalcaemia and her persistent delirium, she was initiated on a modified SLED (slow low efficiency haemodialysis) regimen with a low calcium (1 mmol/L) containing dialysate. After receiving 4 h of SLED on Day 5 and the same on Day 6, her serum calcium level had corrected to within normal limits and her delirious state had dramatically improved. Upon stabilization of her condition in the ICU, she was transferred to the oncology department where chemotherapy and combination antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine/lamivudine/efavirenz) were initiated. Unfortunately she demised a month later from chemotherapy associated neutropenia and septic shock.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-positive woman was admitted to the intensive care unit with a generalized maculopapular rash, polyarthralgia/joint swelling, high fever, fatigue, and acute delirium.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV-1 in 2006 and never started on ART per prior local guidelines because her CD4+ counts consistently remained >500 cells/µL, the patient developed acute fever, fatigue, generalized skin rash, painful swelling of the knees, elbows, and ankles, and delirium.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection diagnosed in 2006 (ART-naive with preserved CD4+ counts >500 cells/µL).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized maculopapular rash, knee/elbow/ankle joint pain and swelling, high fever, fatigue, and delirium.

objective.physical_examination: Acutely ill and delirious (without focal neurological deficits) with high fever (39.1 °C), a generalized maculopapular skin rash, marked symmetric swelling of the bilateral knee, elbow, and ankle joints, axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy, and 4 cm splenomegaly without hepatomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory workup revealed severe life-threatening hypercalcemia (serum calcium 4.48 mmol/L) and strongly positive HTLV-1 serology, while CBC, renal and liver function tests, blood and urine cultures, autoimmune screen, serum protein electrophoresis, urinary Bence-Jones protein, serum ACE, intact PTH, beta-2 microglobulin, synovial fluid analysis, and respiratory viral PCR were unremarkable.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 616 cells/µL. Whole-body CT demonstrated extensive axillary, inguinal, pelvic, and para-aortic lymphadenopathy; radioisotope bone scan showed increased juxta-articular uptake at the elbows and knees. Skin biopsy showed vasculitic infiltration by atypical T-lymphocytes, and excisional lymph node biopsy along with bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy confirmed acute adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: HTLV-1-associated acute adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) presenting with severe paraneoplastic hypercalcemic crisis (4.48 mmol/L) and delirium in a 37-year-old woman with untreated HIV-1 co-infection (plasma HIV viral load 102,000 copies/mL, CD4+ count 616 cells/µL; confirmed by strongly positive HTLV-1 serology and skin, lymph node, and bone marrow biopsies). Because her hypercalcemia and delirium were refractory to 4 days of high-volume normal saline diuresis, intravenous furosemide (80 mg q12h), intravenous hydrocortisone (100 mg q8h), and zoledronic acid (4 mg IV), she underwent two 4-hour sessions of low-calcium (1 mmol/L) sustained low-efficiency dialysis (SLED) on days 5 and 6, achieving normocalcemia and complete resolution of delirium. She was transferred to oncology and initiated on systemic chemotherapy and cART (zidovudine/lamivudine/efavirenz), but died 1 month later from chemotherapy-induced febrile neutropenia and septic shock.
